pr_body:
#94133 changed watcher to load watcher history asynchronously. So if a test runs a watch and immediately checks the watcher history index, it might not yet have data. This makes sure that we wait for the history index to become green, and wait for non-zero results from it. It's similar to #95642

Closes #94836
Closes #65064
pr_title: Waiting for watcher history index to be populated

review_comment: Is the `ensureGreen` inside the `assertBusy` because the index may not exist (and would throw an assertion failure?)

Yes. I haven't actually seen it on this test, but the test in https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/95642 failed because it tried to query the index before the shards were allocated. I figured no harm in checking that here -- it might save us from a rare test failure.
And I think if we try to query the index before shards are allocated it will throw an uncaught exception rather than an assertion failure, so the assertBusy block would fail.
